title: Chapter 195: Tian Teng Medical School's Haunting Past
html:
At the woman’s words, the hairs rose visibly along the man’s neck. Chen Ge had imitated the note’s handwriting as a prank, never expecting such an extreme reaction.

Eyes narrowed, he positioned himself between the actors and the recorder. Tian Teng Medical School might be more than it appeared; perhaps it truly was haunted.

Xing Hai was a major city, and Tian Teng Medical School had invested heavily in establishing itself there. Yet after only weeks of operation, the attraction had departed in haste for distant Jiujiang.

If they knew her name might summon her spirit, why keep using it?Chen Ge could not understand the proprietor’s reasoning. Did he think moving would leave the ghost behind, or does Xu Zhenzhen mean something special to him?

In the dim light, the actor brought the note close to his face. “The ink is still wet.”

He glanced at Chen Ge, then quickly looked away. “We’ve had only one visitor. Even if he brought a pen and wrote this, how do we explain the voice in the recorder? This scene is new; only the design team knows the recorder exists. Who visits a Haunted House carrying a cassette tape?”

As he spoke, another scream erupted from the recorder. Its suffering sounded utterly different from the staged voice. Even through a small speaker, it made every listener shudder, as though a murder were unfolding beside them.

“Brother Lin…” The female actor moved toward the door. “How come the recording sounds so real?”

“I have no idea.” The man glanced back and found Chen Ge still beside the recorder. After a moment’s hesitation, he ignored him and hurried to the woman. “Besides this note, did you find anything else unusual in your room?”

“No.”

“What about the others?”

“They should arrive soon.” Her eyes darted around, and she seemed close to breaking. “Did that thing come back? We only just reopened. Didn’t the boss say he had dealt with it?”

“What are you talking about? What happened here?” Chen Ge lifted the recorder, intending to persuade them to let him carry it outside. The sight of him holding it made both actors freeze.

“Put that thing down!” the female actor demanded shrilly. “We did not record the voice that is coming out of it now!”

Of course, Chen Ge knew that, but he could not admit that he knew. “The recorder is inside your Haunted House. If you didn’t record this tape, who did? Are you telling me that a ghost did?”

The man had no answer. Ignoring his attempt to stop her, the woman stepped forward. “In Xing Hai, one visitor fled in tears. She said one of our actresses had been terrifyingly convincing—but no actor was assigned to that location. When she described the woman, every detail matched Xu Zhenzhen.”

“Maybe the visitor was playing a prank on you?” Chen Ge asked with a weird expression. “She might have been kidding.”

“It happened repeatedly. After that day, more visitors began seeing Xu Zhenzhen.” The man pulled a Buddha pendant from beneath his shirt. “Every employee carries something for protection, yet strangely, none of us has ever seen her.”

“If the haunting is real, why fill the attraction with references to Xu Zhenzhen? Aren’t you afraid of calling her back?” Chen Ge thought they must have lost their minds. “Or is this still part of the performance? Are the note and recording tricks meant to frighten me?”

“I swear to God, we’re not acting,” both actors promised.

“You have to understand. Xing Hai was our first stop, so we based the set on a real local case to make it more frightening and attract visitors. Xu Zhenzhen’s suicide is infamous there. Seeing her name immediately calls the case to mind.”

The man looked ill. “We had little choice. Attendance had declined for two years despite our experimenting with different set designs. To preserve our popularity, we needed something new.”

“So you built the attraction around a real tragedy?” These people seemed even more reckless than Chen Ge. At least he prepared safeguards for everything he did.

“It worked. Our reputation and attendance rose steadily. After discovering the clues, many visitors returned to unravel Xu Zhenzhen’s secret.”

“If business was thriving, why come to Jiujiang? Wouldn’t staying in Xing Hai have been more profitable?” The recorder continued screaming in Chen Ge’s arms, though he seemed not to notice. The actors stared at him, speechless. When he stepped forward, both retreated in perfect unison.

“Reports that visitors saw Xu Zhenzhen became excellent publicity. We enjoyed tremendous popularity for a while, but fame had a price. Her family grew furious, and her younger sister confronted us.”

As the woman revealed Tian Teng Medical School’s history, Chen Ge finally managed to silence the recorder.

“During negotiations, Xu Zhenzhen’s sister accused us of tarnishing her family’s name. She demanded substantial compensation and a complete redesign.

“Our boss agreed only to remove Xu Zhenzhen’s name. Compensation and a total redesign were out of the question. She threatened to sue. I don’t know what followed, but the Haunted House closed soon afterward.”

The woman appeared truthful. Large traveling Haunted Houses struggled to obtain official approval and could easily be shut down after a dispute. Chen Ge knew this because his parents had once operated a mobile attraction, settling in New Century Park only after building sufficient popularity.

“We packed the props, changed the layout and name, and moved to another city. The results were disastrous. Attendance vanished within two weeks. We concluded that removing Xu Zhenzhen was the problem, so we relocated far from Xing Hai to Jiujiang and restored the attraction to its most successful version.”

The two actors had already retreated to the door. Looking at Chen Ge, who held the tape recorder, they had revealed everything.
